title: Draft initial Originium frame catalog
description: Why this issue exists: Frame schema work needs concrete examples before it hardens into the wrong abstraction, but the first catalog should remain a small advisory vocabulary rather than a complete ontology. What needs to be done: draft the initial Originium frame catalog from the Cisco industrial source corpus and CURWB mining fixture, covering bounded Source Document classes and Wiki Page roles such as design guide, implementation guide, solution brief, white paper, concept, requirement set, procedure, technology component, reference architecture, deployment pattern, use case, and operational risk.
acceptance_criteria: A docs-level initial frame catalog exists before schema implementation depends on it; each frame has a scope note, examples, non-examples where useful, and recommended metadata slots; the catalog is explicitly sparse/advisory and not a closed ontology; examples come from the current Cisco corpus and CURWB mining fixture; runtime seed data is optional and should be added only after the schema shape exists.

title: Add frame metadata CLI workflows
description: Why this issue exists: Agents need repeatable CLI affordances to inspect frames, assign frames, set frame metadata, and validate metadata without hand-writing arbitrary JSON. What needs to be done: add commands for listing/showing frames, assigning a frame to a Source Document or Wiki Page, setting frame-scoped metadata slots, validating metadata against frame definitions, and explaining missing/recommended fields.
acceptance_criteria: CLI supports frame list/show, frame assign, metadata set/show/validate or equivalent; errors name operation/input/reason/action; commands work for Source Documents and Wiki Pages; metadata validation is advisory by default and can report missing recommended slots without blocking writes; tests cover valid, partial, unknown-slot, and invalid-type metadata.

title: Add frame-guided Source Document metadata
description: Why this issue exists: Source Documents need frontmatter-like metadata for retrieval, filtering, UI grouping, and citation display, but completely free-form metadata will drift. What needs to be done: add Source Document metadata fields or a metadata object governed by document frames/classes, with CLI support to set, inspect, and validate corpus, publisher, document class, industries, product families, version, publication date, source URL, and trust status when known.
acceptance_criteria: Source Document metadata can be stored, read, updated, and validated; import can accept or infer basic metadata where practical; metadata supports sparse documents; CLI output distinguishes missing metadata from invalid metadata; tests cover common Cisco corpus metadata and unknown/partial metadata.

title: Replace page_kind with Wiki Page frame metadata
description: Why this issue exists: The current page_kind enum cannot represent Originium's actual knowledge objects such as requirement sets, procedures, technology components, reference architectures, deployment patterns, use cases, and operational risks. What needs to be done: replace or supersede page_kind with frame assignment plus frame-scoped metadata on Wiki Pages, while preserving existing pages through migration or compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Wiki Pages can be assigned a Domain Frame and sparse frame metadata; existing page_kind values migrate or remain compatible; page create/update/read/search expose frame metadata; lint reports missing high-value frame metadata without blocking ordinary page creation; tests cover concept, procedure, requirement set, component, and reference architecture examples.

title: Align docs on frame-guided metadata ownership
description: Why this issue exists: CONTEXT.md, SPEC.md, docs/learning-graph-spec.md, access-pattern docs, ADRs, and the graph-wiki skill currently disagree about Source Headings, Source Anchors, free-form metadata, Manual Links, and where semantic metadata belongs. What needs to be done: update the product language and planning docs so Source Document metadata, projection metadata, Wiki Page frame metadata, Citation locator metadata, Domain Frames, and Manual Links have clear ownership boundaries. Explicitly state that frames define relevant metadata slots and remain advisory, not a strict ontology that blocks ingestion.
acceptance_criteria: Docs define Domain Frame/Domain Schema terminology; Source Heading and Source Anchor are removed from the product language rather than demoted to semantic graph entities; Source Text Projections are described as Source Document-owned per-page caches for paginated sources, with whole-document text derived from ordered page projections unless future performance evidence justifies a separate cache; metadata ownership is described for Source Documents, projections, Wiki Pages, Citations, Frames, and Manual Links; overcomplicated contradiction/evidence-only/relation-search features are marked as skill guidance or deferred.
close_reason: Aligned canonical docs and graph-wiki skill around frame-guided metadata ownership, citation locator scope, restricted Manual Link semantics, and POC rebuild policy instead of migration.

title: Add minimal Domain Frame and metadata slot schema
description: Why this issue exists: Wiki Page page_kind is too small and free-form metadata is too loose. Originium needs advisory frames that define relevant metadata slots without enforcing a complete ontology ahead of time. What needs to be done: add the minimal schema support needed for Domain Frames, frame-defined metadata slots, frame assignments, and audit/provenance fields. Keep relation-label governance, model proposals, and full version migration workflows out of this first schema slice unless another accepted bead requires them.
acceptance_criteria: Schema includes Domain Frame records, metadata slot definitions, and a frame assignment representation for Source Documents and Wiki Pages; slot definitions can mark required/recommended/optional fields and basic value kinds; frame records carry review/status and creation/update provenance sufficient for audit; frame metadata remains sparse and advisory by default; relation-label registries, Domain Model proposal workflows, and full model versioning are explicitly deferred; tests cover sparse, unknown-slot, invalid-type, and reviewed-frame cases.

title: Epic: Frame-guided metadata model
description: Why this issue exists: Originium needs a clearer answer to where semantic metadata belongs. Completely free-form metadata is too loose, but a strict up-front ontology would over-constrain source ingestion. Frames should define relevant metadata slots for each kind of Wiki Page and Source Document while staying advisory enough for agents to evolve the graph. What needs to be done: introduce a frame-guided metadata model across docs, schema, CLI, skill, retrieval, and UI so Source Documents carry frontmatter-like provenance metadata, Wiki Pages get frame-defined semantic metadata, Citations carry evidence locator metadata, and Manual Links remain rare navigational edges rather than the primary semantic model.
acceptance_criteria: Frames define metadata slots for Source Documents and Wiki Pages; source metadata supports corpus/document-class filtering; Wiki Page page_kind is replaced or superseded by frame assignment plus frame-scoped metadata; citation metadata remains evidence/locator focused; Manual Link labels are restricted or deferred; docs, graph-wiki skill, schema, CLI, tests, and UI agree on the metadata ownership model.
notes: Migration scope update: current proof-of-concept graph may be rebuilt from Source Documents/projections/catalog data. Do not implement a compatibility migration for existing local records as part of this epic; future durable deployments need a separate migration design before incompatible schema changes.

title: Update access-pattern docs for simplified citation model
description: Why this issue exists: docs/access-patterns still describe Source Headings and Source Anchors as first-class citation targets, but current planning has decided to remove them and simplify citation around Source Documents plus citation-local locator fields. What needs to be done: revise the access-pattern docs to reflect the simplified graph model, demote extracted headings/sections to projection metadata, and remove stale guidance that asks agents to cite Source Headings or create Source Anchors.
close_reason: Updated docs/access-patterns to reflect the simplified Source Document plus citation-local locator model and demoted extracted headings/sections to projection metadata.

title: Remove Source Anchor concept entirely
description: Why this issue exists: Source Anchor is redundant once Citations target Source Documents directly with citation-local locator metadata. Keeping Source Anchor would preserve the same over-modeled evidence indirection as Source Heading under a different name. What needs to be done: remove Source Anchor from the conceptual model, schema, CLI command surface, docs, and graph-wiki skill; migrate any useful anchor location fields into Citation locator metadata; reserve any future reusable evidence-span concept for a later design only if real workflows prove it is needed.
acceptance_criteria: Source Anchor is no longer defined in product language, schema, CLI workflows, docs, or graph-wiki skill guidance; source anchor create/read/search commands are removed or clearly deprecated; citation locator fields cover document-level, page-range, quote/context, projection identity, and validation metadata directly on Citation relations; migration or compatibility path handles existing source_anchor records; citation lint reports missing or broad locators without relying on Source Anchors.
notes: Docs-only slice updated: current product/architecture/graph-wiki text no longer defines Source Anchor as a target concept; citation precision belongs in Citation locator metadata. Legacy exact-term references are limited to legacy inspection/cleanup docs. No code/schema/package/test edits by this agent.
close_reason: Removed Source Anchor from schema/domain/CLI/docs target model; citation precision now lives on Citation locator metadata with deprecated CLI path.

title: Remove Source Heading concept entirely
description: Why this issue exists: Source Heading is over-modeled and should not remain as a domain concept, citation target, graph node, or projection boundary. For paginated Source Documents, source text should be stored as rebuildable per-page Source Text Projections, not as section/heading entities or persisted whole-document blocks. What needs to be done: remove Source Heading from the conceptual model, schema, CLI command surface, web graph neighborhood assumptions, docs, and graph-wiki skill; migrate citations and projections to Source Document plus citation-local locator fields; delete or explicitly deprecate source_heading records and commands rather than replacing them with another section ontology.
acceptance_criteria: Source Heading is no longer defined in CONTEXT.md, SPEC.md, architecture docs, or graph-wiki skill guidance; schema and CLI workflows no longer require source_heading records; Source Text Projections are keyed to Source Documents and stored per page for paginated Source Documents rather than as heading/section or persisted whole-document blocks; Citation relations target Source Documents and carry citation-local locator fields; source search/projection commands do not require heading ids; web graph-neighborhood code no longer treats Source Headings as selectable graph nodes; migration or compatibility path handles existing source_heading and cites records explicitly.
notes: Docs-only slice updated: current product/architecture/graph-wiki text now treats extracted headings as locator/projection metadata, not target domain concepts; citations target Source Documents with citation-local locator metadata; paginated Source Text Projections are per-page rebuildable caches. Legacy source_heading references remain only in explicitly marked legacy inspection/cleanup docs. No code/schema/package/test edits by this agent.
close_reason: Removed Source Heading from schema/domain/CLI/web/docs target model; projections are Source Document/page keyed and legacy references are explicit.

title: Add MVP bundled answer context workflow
description: Why this issue exists: Answering from the graph currently requires agents to manually compose page search, retrieval search, page read, citation list, citation validation, graph neighborhood, and source search. That composition should be a CLI-owned access pattern, but the first slice should return the evidence bundle needed for responsible answers rather than a general retrieval platform. What needs to be done: upgrade or replace workflow answer-context with an MVP command that gathers maintained Wiki Page synthesis, citation status, cited Source Document locators, relevant source projections/snippets, and explicit gaps/warnings.
acceptance_criteria: answer context returns candidate Wiki Pages, page bodies, citation validation status, cited Source Documents with locator evidence, relevant source snippets/projections, and explicit gaps/warnings; output distinguishes maintained synthesis from raw source evidence; retrieval trace and graph neighborhood are included only when existing commands already expose them cheaply, otherwise they are deferred to follow-up beads; tests cover complete, thin, missing, and conflicting-source context cases.
close_reason: Upgraded workflow answer-context to return maintained synthesis, citation evidence, raw source snippets, warnings, gaps, and optional trace.

title: Add source locator and diagnostics commands
description: Why this issue exists: Agents need the CLI to identify whether source material is missing, imported but unindexed, indexed but missing projections, or present with no matching evidence. Current source commands expose pieces of this but still assume heading-oriented evidence. What needs to be done: add source find, locate, diagnostics, and traced evidence commands that operate over Source Documents and per-page Source Text Projections for paginated sources without requiring Source Heading or Source Anchor records.
acceptance_criteria: source find resolves Source Documents by path, title, fingerprint, and corpus metadata; source locate maps page or page-range plus quote/context input to document-local locators and per-page projection spans; source diagnostics reports import, extraction, per-page projection, embedding, and citation-locator health without treating sections/headings as graph entities; source evidence --trace records queries, filters, scores, and rejected near misses over Source Documents and Source Text Projections; whole-document text is derived from ordered page projections rather than persisted for PDFs.

title: Add Source Document citation locator model and cite workflow
description: Why this issue exists: Agents cannot be expected to hand-write perfect citation records. Current Citation relations only store key, label, and quote, and the old model routes citations through Source Heading/Source Anchor records that should be removed. What needs to be done: extend the citation model so Citation relations target Source Documents directly and carry citation-local locator fields; add a first-class cite workflow that accepts a Source Document plus optional locator input and produces a validated Citation relation.
acceptance_criteria: Schema supports Citation relations from Wiki Pages to Source Documents with citation-local claim, locator kind, optional page range, optional location hint, quote/context, optional projection id, text hash, validation status, and confidence; locator kind can represent whole-document, page-range, and quote/context evidence without requiring headings or anchors; originium cite create creates validated Citation edges from Source Document locator input; existing citation add remains compatible or is clearly superseded; tests cover whole-document citation, page-range citation, quote/context citation, and concrete validation failures.

title: Add rich citation validation and repair commands
description: Why this issue exists: Current citation validation mostly checks Page Body markers against graph Citation keys. Agents need the CLI to validate locator correctness, stale projections, overly broad or missing source-document locators, and unsupported claims before answers or refactors rely on them. What needs to be done: Expand citation validation and add repair/narrowing commands for common citation problems.
acceptance_criteria: citation validate/lint verifies marker matching, target existence, page range coverage, quote/context against projection when possible, projection hash freshness, broad or missing locator risk, and claim metadata; citation narrow updates locator fields without changing the supported claim; citation repair can retarget or mark unsupported claims with concrete before/after output.

description: Why this issue exists: The access-pattern docs clarified that agents should provide semantic judgment while the CLI owns exact graph mutation, citation precision, validation, refactors, and index consistency. The current CLI has useful low-level commands, but agents still need to manually compose fragile operations. What needs to be done: build the Graph Wiki foundation CLI command families needed for source indexing, question answering, graph maintenance, citation-safe refactors, and frame-guided metadata while deferring learner-specific graph workflows.

title: Milestone: Graph-native multi-document retrieval foundation ready
description:
Final state: Originium has a graph-native retrieval and indexing foundation suitable for parallel indexing and query agents over the Cisco corpus and future multi-document Source Documents.

Expected state:
- Source Documents remain immutable canonical evidence.
- Source Text Projections exist as lossy, rebuildable search caches with provenance, page ranges, extractor metadata, and hashes.
- Wiki Pages and Source Text Projections have persisted embeddings and SurrealDB full-text/vector indexes.
- Retrieval uses SurrealDB hybrid candidate search plus graph-aware reranking instead of brute-force live embedding of every candidate.
- Indexer agents have page-candidate tooling and page metadata that support concept reuse, alias discovery, broadening existing pages, and duplicate avoidance.
- Query agents can use separate workflows for answer retrieval, evidence search, and graph neighborhood traversal.
- Manual Links use disciplined labels plus concrete reasons so graph traversal is useful without schema fragmentation.
- Architecture docs and the graph-wiki skill describe the intended middle path between overly normalized graph fragments and overly organized human documents.

This milestone is reached after the graph-native retrieval foundation closeout passes or explicitly records named blockers and follow-up beads.
acceptance_criteria: Milestone can be closed when originium-9ou.13 is closed and its closeout evidence proves or explicitly classifies every final-state bullet above.
close_reason: Milestone reached: originium-9ou.13 closeout proves or classifies every final-state bullet and records follow-up beads for deferred file API and Source Anchor citation work.

title: Validate staged POC acceptance harness semantics
description:
Description:
Validate the staged acceptance harness itself before relying on it as POC proof.

Scenario:
- The harness can run while some stages are unimplemented and still distinguish pass, fail, blocked, deferred, and not-applicable states.

Procedure:
- Run the harness on a clean checkout before all POC features are complete.
- Inspect stage output and exit code behavior.

Required evidence:
- Each stage reports a result state and concrete reason.

Pass criteria:
- The harness exits nonzero only for in-scope failures, not for explicitly deferred unimplemented stages.

Failure classification:
- Ambiguous skipped stages or misleading zero exits are harness failures.

Recommended skill: validate-behavior
acceptance_criteria: Harness validation proves staged result states and correct exit behavior for deferred versus failing POC stages.
close_reason: Validated staged acceptance harness semantics with focused CLI test: blocked SurrealDB stages emit blocked state and nonzero exit; deferred and not-applicable stages are explicit.

title: Validate chapter ingestion workflow
description:
Description:
Validate chapter-by-chapter ingestion as the agent workflow for massive PDFs.

Scenario:
- An agent processes one Source Heading from the fixture without loading the whole PDF into context.

title: [SPIKE] Evaluate real SurrealDB file bucket API usage
description: [SPIKE]\\nWhy this exists: current Source Document import defines a SurrealDB file bucket but copies PDFs directly into the host-local bucket directory and streams them by path. This is acceptable for host-direct POC but limits remote SurrealDB, workers, and durable service boundaries.\\n\\nQuestion to answer:\\n- Can Originium use SurrealDB file-management APIs for Source Document upload/read with the current SurrealDB version and host-direct runtime?\\n\\nScope:\\n- Inspect SurrealDB file API behavior and current TypeScript client/HTTP/RPC options.\\n- Prototype or document the minimal upload/read path if practical.\\n- Recommend follow-up implementation beads or explicitly classify why host-direct file path fallback remains necessary.\\n\\nOut of scope:\\n- Rewriting import/streaming unless the spike proves it is trivial and low risk.\\n\\nAgent-factory route: audit
acceptance_criteria: Spike records whether SurrealDB file APIs can replace direct bucket-directory copies/reads now, lists required code/config changes, identifies compatibility risks, and creates follow-up implementation bead(s) if the answer is yes or a documented deferral if not.
notes: Audit result (2026-05-17): PARTIAL. Originium can use SurrealDB file bucket APIs in the current SurrealDB generation for metadata/file operations, but the current host-direct runtime cannot replace direct bucket-directory PDF copy/read without code/config changes. Evidence: local surreal version is 3.0.5; packages/surreal starts SurrealDB with SURREAL_CAPS_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL=files and SURREAL_BUCKET_FOLDER_ALLOWLIST=config.bucketDir; sourceDocumentBucketSurql defines DEFINE BUCKET IF NOT EXISTS source_documents BACKEND "file:<bucketDir>". Current import still mkdir/copyFileSyncs the PDF into config.bucketDir and stores a plain object {bucket,key,pointer}; current web streaming reads config.sourcePdf.bucketDir with fs createReadStream after selecting metadata. No @surrealdb/surrealdb or surrealdb JS SDK dependency is installed; current DB client only POSTs SurrealQL text to /sql. Official SurrealDB docs consulted: DEFINE BUCKET is available since v3.0.0, experimental, requires --allow-experimental files or SURREAL_CAPS_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL=files; file pointers support put/get/head/list/delete/copy/rename; FileRef exists in the JS SDK; HTTP /sql accepts SurrealQL text and URL query params; default SURREAL_HTTP_MAX_SQL_BODY_SIZE is 1 MiB and SURREAL_HTTP_MAX_RPC_BODY_SIZE is 4 MiB while WebSocket max message size is 128 MiB. Compatibility assessment: host-direct can keep defining buckets and can likely use file::head/list/get for smaller reads through SurrealQL, but real PDF upload through current /sql wrapper is not practical for existing large PDFs without either adding a binary-capable RPC/SDK path or raising HTTP limits and encoding bytes into SurrealQL. Read streaming through SurrealDB would also need a backend helper that returns bytes from f"bucket:/key".get() or a real SDK FileRef path; otherwise host-local fs streaming remains the only proven efficient path. Required changes if proceeding: add a Surreal file service in packages/surreal; add a binary-capable client path (official JS SDK/RPC over WebSocket, or explicit HTTP/RPC implementation with vars); store actual file pointer/FileRef-compatible values instead of plain object pointer strings or normalize reads around them; change CLI import to put bytes via Surreal instead of copyFileSync; change web source PDF streaming to read via Surreal for remote DB mode while keeping host-direct fs fallback; configure/validate size limits and experimental file capability. Risk: Surreal file buckets are still experimental and docs say subject to change; SDK/docs are moving around v3 and FileRef support requires adding a new dependency; HTTP defaults are too small for current 27MB PDFs; remote SurrealDB with file backend still needs server-side storage/allowlist/global bucket policy, so it does not by itself solve object-storage durability. Follow-up recommendation: create an implementation spike or feature bead for a Surreal file service with a tiny text/binary fixture first, then a large-PDF upload/read validation; keep host-direct file path fallback until that passes.
close_reason: Spike classified real Surreal file API usage as partial/deferred for current host-direct runtime, recorded required changes and risks, and filed follow-up originium-ph2.

What needs to be done: keep first-pass Domain Model behavior inside the smaller frame schema and frame CLI beads, and defer relation-label search, model proposal/version commands, and automatic migrations until real frame workflows show the missing shape.
acceptance_criteria: Frame list/show/assign/validate behavior is owned by the frame metadata schema and CLI beads; this bead records that relation-label registries, model proposal commands, model version commands, model impact analysis, and model migrate --dry-run are not part of the first frame MVP; any revived Domain Model primitive must have a concrete workflow, examples from graph state, and its own implementation bead; no implementation work is required here beyond updating docs/skill text if they still imply the broader command surface.
notes: Docs-only slice updated: Domain Model relation-label search, model-impact, versioning, and migration dry-run primitives are explicitly deferred until frame workflow MVP proves concrete need. No code/schema/package/test edits by this agent.
close_reason: Docs and graph-wiki skill now defer broad Domain Model primitives behind frame workflow MVP; no implementation work required beyond updated guidance.

title: Plan split deployment and containerization after host-direct handoff
description:
## Purpose
Track future deployment work that was intentionally deferred until the host-direct web app milestone was proven.

## Scope
Define and implement explicit service, storage, credential, job/session, and validation contracts required before Originium can move beyond the single-host topology. Cover remote SurrealDB operation, frontend/backend split, agent-worker split, and container packaging only after the host-direct assumptions are replaced.

## Out of Scope
Changing the current host-direct runtime, weakening the browser/backend trust boundary, or adding containers as a wrapper around unresolved local filesystem/process assumptions.

## Context
`docs/architecture/index.md`, `SPEC.md`, ADR 0003, and ADR 0004 describe the current host-direct topology and the prerequisites for split deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Future work is complete when Originium has explicit contracts and validation for remote SurrealDB/file-bucket storage, frontend/backend API and auth/origin policy, durable agent worker job/session/activity streaming, credential handling, and container or split-deployment packaging; each implementation slice has its own executable beads before work starts.

title: Add basic Source Document import entry point
description:
Purpose: provide a simple web path for adding Source Documents once backend upload semantics are ready.

Scope: minimal PDF upload/import control that calls backend/CLI semantics, reports operation progress/failure, and refreshes the Source Document list.

Out of scope: URL import, bulk import, OCR, and advanced metadata editing.

Agent-factory route: implement
acceptance_criteria: A user can import a PDF from /sources or the bead records a concrete blocker if upload/file-bucket semantics are not ready; success creates a Source Document visible in the list and failures name operation/input/reason/action.
notes: Closeout classification 2026-05-16: deferred enhancement, not a dependency of Source Document Page/PDF reading closeout. Parent originium-3j8 acceptance says the user can choose an imported PDF Source Document; it does not require creating a new import from /sources. This bead remains the tracked P3 web upload/import entry point when backend upload semantics are ready.

title: Build Originium human-facing app after POC
description:

In scope:

close_reason: Superseded by closed milestone originium-ogo. The host-direct human-facing app now exists and was validated through originium-ros/originium-zfx; remaining work is tracked by concrete follow-ups including originium-05x for Source Document import UI, originium-iv7 for split deployment/containerization, and the open quality gate bugs originium-dlg, originium-kxi, originium-473, and originium-5iv.

title: Milestone: Learning graph capability
description: Define and implement the CLI-first learning graph capability described in docs/learning-graph-spec.md. The milestone preserves Originium's primary goal of answering questions from curated sources while adding a separate learner graph and learning query workflows over the source-backed Domain Graph.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Domain Graph concept roles and pedagogical relationships are modeled with provenance and confidence. 2. Learner Graph state is stored separately from Domain Graph records. 3. CLI workflows can inspect concept structure, record learner observations, and choose a next learning step. 4. Existing answer retrieval can use concept graph signals without replacing citation-backed evidence.
notes: Plan refinement 2026-05-21: learner graph implementation is deferred. Near-term work should finish Graph Wiki foundations first: Source Document citations, projection/search model, frame metadata, answer context, lint, and migration. Do not start learner-state or learn-next workflows until a new planning pass reactivates this milestone.

title: Assess reusable agent OS extraction after POC evidence
description:
Description:
Use POC evidence to decide whether the Originium agent factory should be extracted into reusable agent OS assets and what those assets would own.

In scope:
- Review implemented CLI, skills, schema, logging, ingestion workflow, validation evidence, and orchestrator experience.
- Separate reusable workflow patterns from Originium-specific product assumptions.
- Compare distribution options: repo-local copy, script-managed sync, symlink, Codex plugin, or future Codex feature.

Out of scope:
- Building packaging before the POC is proven.
- Changing POC architecture to satisfy hypothetical reuse.

Recommended skill: architecture-audit
acceptance_criteria: A follow-up decision or backlog captures whether reusable agent OS extraction is useful, with concrete boundaries and distribution tradeoffs.

title: Validate later reusable agent OS extraction
description:
Description:
Track deferred investigation into whether the repo-local agent factory should be extracted into a reusable agent operating system after Originium proves the workflow.

In scope:
- Identify what remains generic across projects versus what is Originium-specific binding.
- Validate whether Codex plugin packaging, direct skill copying, symlinks, or another distribution path is least bad after real usage.
- Capture risks around session-scoped enablement, skill discoverability, local tool dependencies, and update workflow.

Out of scope:
- Blocking POC ingestion or retrieval work.
- Reintroducing a plugin before repo-local skills prove useful.

Recommended skill: manage-beads
acceptance_criteria: After the POC acceptance test passes, produce a decision or implementation backlog for reusable agent OS extraction, or explicitly close as not worth doing.
